name: @chatvault/mobile
comment: @expo/metro-runtime, react-native-worklets and @react-native/metro-config are listed as
dependencies only to pin them. Nothing here imports any of the three directly — all are
reached solely through unpinned peer deps (expo-router, @expo/ui, react-native-reanimated),
so pnpm was free to pick its own versions and picked badly, with no error until the app died
at launch:
@expo/metro-runtime resolved to 4.0.1 while Expo SDK 57 requires ^57.0.11. Its
messageSocket.native.ts opens a dev websocket at module scope during startup, so the
mismatch surfaced as `[runtime not ready]: TypeError: Object is not a function` with no
stack and no named module — the app was simply dead on every launch.
react-native-worklets resolved to 0.11.4 although expo-modules-core@57.0.11 declares
support only up to ^0.10.0. 0.10.4 is the newest version all three consumers accept.
@react-native/metro-config resolved to 0.87.0 (2026-09-17, after bumping expo to 57.0.23
for the iOS 27 UIScene launch-crash fix) although react-native@0.86.3's own
@react-native/community-cli-plugin declares a peer on exactly 0.86.3 — pnpm's dedup picked
the newer sibling package instead of the one react-native itself needs.
Re-check all three on any Expo SDK bump, and prefer `expo install --check` over bare versions.
expo-glass-effect and react-native-safe-area-context are pinned for the opposite reason: both
ARE imported (components/app/Glass.tsx, the tab bar, the tutorial), and both were already in
the native binary through expo-router before this app named them. They are pinned to exactly
the versions the lockfile had resolved for expo-router (57.0.3 and 5.9.0), so that naming
them changes what Metro can resolve and nothing about what is compiled into the app: builds
that take JS over the air (expo-updates, runtimeVersion = app version) already contain this
native code — as long as they were built from this lockfile, which last changed on
2026-09-19, before 0.1.1. Glass.tsx falls back to an opaque view if the module is missing
all the same. `expo install --check` calls both pins outdated; do not bump either without a
new store build.
